scope: Exact-width native word FLAGS and protected legacy PUSHF/PUSHFD/POPF/POPFD

instruction_contract.reference_revision: Intel SDM 093, Volume 2, POPF/POPFD/POPFQ and PUSHF/PUSHFD/PUSHFQ
instruction_contract.protected_runtime: Explicit ordinary RAM in code16/code32, legacy paging and PAE, independent operand and SS.B stack widths; original CPL/IOPL controls IF and IOPL; word POPF preserves AC/ID; PVI does not redirect IF to VIF.
instruction_contract.faults: Complete operand admission uses old AC and privilege state. Register/flags/SP commit is staged; earlier page-table effects remain observable. Original handlers repair PTEs, discard error codes and IRET/retry. CPL0 cannot retry when its fault-entry stack is itself unavailable and reaches the qualified shutdown outcome.
instruction_contract.native_compiler: New llvm.x86.flags.{read,write}.u16 and Clang/NeverC builtins use exact two-byte push/pop. Conservative memory/flag effects, unused reads, frame/red-zone ownership, i386/x64 and LLVM code16 code generation are checked.
instruction_contract.c_emitters: MedLLVM, HighC and LLVMC share the width inventory. New builtins are preferred; older compilers use exact word GNU assembly. The x64 fallback moves RSP with LEA around the red zone and evaluates the input once.
instruction_contract.cpu_witness: Original raw word POPF is compared with unchanged emitted C and native compiler/object output. All 32768 TF-clear word images and four AC/ID inputs are covered at O0/O2 on P/E cores. System flags mask 0x247600 is compared; ordinary C ABI arithmetic flags are deliberately not claimed. Assembly restores host flags before returning to C.
instruction_contract.i386_boundary: Full LLVM/Clang and NeverD ELF32 native/source output execute with the cdecl witness and multilib libc. NeverC remains x64-only. LLVM code16 uses its 32-bit pointer/stack ABI, not an arbitrary original protected-machine state.

neverc_later_integration.unrebuilt_remote_merge_scope: Unrelated C++ translation frontend and its documentation/diagnostic plans. The recorded x86 compiler inputs remain identical.

host.oracle: Independent original instructions in KVM for protected state, and native ELF32/ELF64 for compiler ABI completion.
